stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is considering a nonprescription retail sale of a medicinal preparation that has already been confirmed to qualify for the controlled-substance exception described in M.G.L. c. 94C §4. Which §5 controls still apply to the sale? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The purchaser must identify themself to the pharmacist's satisfaction.
The pharmacist must keep the required purchaser/product sale record.
Because the product qualifies for an exception, any amount may be sold in a single transaction without a time-based limit.
The pharmacist must observe the four-ounce-per-person limit during a 48-hour period.
The sale must be processed as a Schedule II emergency oral prescription.

explanation.core_reasoning: An excepted preparation is not an unrestricted OTC item. The special retail pathway remains conditioned on identification, quantity/time limits, good-faith medicinal sale, and recordkeeping.

choice_analysis.A: Section 5 conditions the retail exception on purchaser identification satisfactory to the pharmacist.
choice_analysis.B: The statute requires an accurate record including purchaser and preparation information.
choice_analysis.C: The exception is conditional; §5 imposes a four-ounce per person/48-hour limit.
choice_analysis.D: This is the quantity/time condition stated in §5.
choice_analysis.E: The special retail exception is not the Schedule II emergency prescription pathway.

related_facts: The question assumes the product already qualifies for the underlying §4 exception.
Section 5 then supplies the retail conditions.
explanation.mpje_trap: An exception from ordinary prescription control can still carry its own purchaser, quantity, and record requirements.

reasoning_steps: Accept the stem's premise that the product qualifies under §4
Distinguish the pathway from ordinary prescription dispensing
